tonight.headline: Allgeier is in the flex now — McLaurin's Saturday report no longer decides anything
body: Bad news first: Terry McLaurin's hamstring status is still unknown. He was limited Thursday and did not practise Friday (a rest day, Washington say), and at 07:00 Saturday Washington had not yet published designations. You already acted on that at 02:35 UTC: Coker to WR, Allgeier to the flex, McLaurin to the bench.

That is the right order. Allgeier and McLaurin project 12.4 each, a coin flip, and Allgeier kicks off Sunday 14:05 while McLaurin plays Monday night. With Allgeier in, there is never a zero to fix. 127.0 projected against Bok-aneers' 112.5; ESPN 57%. Nothing to do before kickoff.

case.label: Why leave it
case.body: A tie on projection carries no thesis, and the order matters: had McLaurin started and been ruled out Monday, Allgeier would already be locked on the bench. Arizona are 12.5-point underdogs at the Rams (SI/FanDuel) — game script that can cut early-down carries, already in ESPN's 12.4.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Allgeier ruled inactive at 12:35 Sunday CDMX (he carries no designation) — then McLaurin back into the flex, if Washington's Saturday report has not ruled him out.

whatWentWrong.title: The lineup tool's McLaurin fallback cannot be executed
whatWentWrong.lead: It says check at Monday 16:45 and start Allgeier — but Allgeier locks Sunday 14:05.

case.label: What happened
case.body: lineup_check.py prints a contingency for McLaurin with a 90-minute-before-kickoff check time, Mon 16:45 CDMX. The fallback it names, Allgeier, plays Sunday at the Rams; by Monday he cannot be moved.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: Nothing today: you have already put Allgeier in, which is the only order where a fallback exists. It matters for every week a Monday or Thursday player is questionable and his cover plays Sunday.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: The tool comparing fallback kickoff against the check time and naming only players still movable — reported as a tool finding this run.
